name: Rice blast
looks_like: Diamond or spindle shaped spots with a grey centre and brown edge on leaves; neck of the panicle turns brown and breaks.
favoured_by: Cool nights, high humidity, heavy nitrogen.
what_to_do: Stop extra nitrogen; split it in small doses next time
Keep the field neat and drain waterlogging
Next season choose a blast-tolerant variety
expert_note: Neck blast can cut yield sharply: show the field to the agriculture officer quickly.

name: Bacterial leaf blight
looks_like: Yellow to straw coloured drying from leaf tips and edges, wavy margins; worse after storms or flooding.
favoured_by: Wind and rain, standing water, heavy nitrogen.
what_to_do: Avoid extra nitrogen
Drain standing water where possible
Do not move through the wet field and then to healthy fields
expert_note: Ask the officer to confirm before spending on any spray.

name: Brown planthopper (hopperburn)
looks_like: Round patches of plants turning yellow then brown and drying; small brown insects at the base of tillers.
favoured_by: Heavy nitrogen, dense planting, humid weather, over-spraying that kills natural enemies.
what_to_do: Look at the base of plants for insects
Drain the field for a few days if possible
Do not spray on your own: wrong sprays make it worse
expert_note: Spreads fast. Call the officer the same day you see patches.

name: Rice stem borer
looks_like: Central shoot dries and pulls out easily (dead heart) early; empty white panicles (whitehead) later.
favoured_by: Continuous paddy, late planting.
what_to_do: Count dead hearts in a few spots to see how widespread
Remove and destroy stubble after harvest
expert_note: The officer can tell if the damage level needs treatment.

name: Zinc deficiency (khaira)
looks_like: Rusty brown spots on middle leaves, stunted uneven growth, often 2 to 4 weeks after transplanting.
favoured_by: Alkaline or repeatedly cropped soil.
what_to_do: Ask for a soil test
Ask the officer about zinc for your soil
expert_note: A soil test gives a certain answer.

name: Leaf spot (tikka disease)
looks_like: Round brown to black spots with a yellow ring on leaves; leaves drop in bad cases.
favoured_by: Humid, cloudy weather and old infected crop residue.
what_to_do: Remove and destroy infected crop residue after harvest
Rotate with a non-legume crop
Use clean seed next season
expert_note: Ask the officer which fungicide is suitable and when.

name: Groundnut rust
looks_like: Orange-brown powdery pustules mainly on the underside of leaves.
favoured_by: Humid weather with warm days.
what_to_do: Check several plants to see how widespread
Destroy volunteer groundnut plants after harvest
expert_note: Confirm with the officer before any spray.

name: Collar rot
looks_like: Young plants suddenly wilt; stem base rots and shows black powdery growth.
favoured_by: Poorly drained or infected soil, seed with injured coat.
what_to_do: Remove wilted plants
Avoid waterlogging
Use healthy, treated seed next time
expert_note: Ask about seed treatment for the next sowing.

name: Bud necrosis (thrips-spread virus)
looks_like: Stunted plants, ring-like spots on young leaves, dying growing tips.
favoured_by: Thrips, dry spells.
what_to_do: Remove badly affected plants early
Keep field edges and bunds free of weeds
expert_note: No cure for the virus; the officer can advise how to reduce thrips.

name: Pink bollworm
looks_like: Flowers twisted into a rosette, bolls with small holes, pink larvae inside seeds, stained lint.
favoured_by: Long-season cotton, leftover bolls and stalks.
what_to_do: Open a few bolls to check for pink larvae
Pick and destroy fallen and rotten bolls
Remove stalks after the last picking
expert_note: Needs a planned control schedule: speak to the agriculture officer.

name: Leaf curl virus (spread by whitefly)
looks_like: Leaves curl upward, veins thicken, plants stunted; whiteflies under leaves and sticky black mould.
favoured_by: Whitefly build-up in warm dry weather.
what_to_do: Look under leaves for whiteflies
Remove badly infected young plants
Keep weeds that host whitefly away
expert_note: Virus cannot be cured; the officer can advise how to control whiteflies.

name: Sucking pests (jassids and aphids)
looks_like: Leaf edges turn yellow then reddish brown and curl downward; tiny green insects under leaves.
favoured_by: Dry weather and too much nitrogen.
what_to_do: Check 10 plants: count insects under leaves
Avoid extra nitrogen
expert_note: Ask the officer if the count is high enough to treat.

name: Anthracnose / fruit rot and die-back
looks_like: Sunken dark spots on ripening fruit, white-grey fruits, twigs drying from the tip.
favoured_by: Warm humid weather, rain at fruiting.
what_to_do: Pick and destroy diseased fruit
Avoid overhead watering
Use clean seed next time
expert_note: The officer can advise on a spray schedule.

name: Wilt / root rot
looks_like: Plants wilt suddenly even with moisture, roots or stem base brown.
favoured_by: Waterlogged soil, repeated same crop.
what_to_do: Remove wilted plants with roots
Improve drainage
Rotate crop next season
expert_note: Ask the officer about soil treatment for the next crop.

name: Early blight
looks_like: Brown spots with ring pattern like a target on older lower leaves.
favoured_by: Warm humid weather, plant stress.
what_to_do: Remove badly infected lower leaves
Water at the base, not on leaves
Stake plants for air flow
expert_note: The officer can suggest a suitable fungicide.

name: Late blight
looks_like: Large dark water-soaked patches on leaves, stems and fruit; white fuzz underneath in humid weather; spreads in days.
favoured_by: Cool, wet, cloudy weather.
what_to_do: Remove and bury badly affected plants
Do not work in the wet field
expert_note: This can destroy a crop in days: call an expert now.

name: Fruit borer (Helicoverpa)
looks_like: Round holes in fruit or bolls, green-brown caterpillar inside, droppings.
favoured_by: Warm weather; flowering and fruiting stage.
what_to_do: Collect and destroy damaged fruit
Hand-pick caterpillars in a small field
expert_note: Ask the officer about traps and control timing.

name: Fall armyworm
looks_like: Ragged holes and windowing in young leaves, sawdust-like droppings in the whorl, caterpillars inside.
favoured_by: Warm weather, staggered sowing in the area.
what_to_do: Check 20 plants and count damaged whorls
Hand-pick caterpillars in small plots
Report to the agriculture officer: it spreads
expert_note: Early action matters; the officer will say what is recommended.

name: Nitrogen shortage
looks_like: Whole plant pale green; oldest lower leaves yellow first, starting at the tip.
favoured_by: Light soils, heavy rain washing nutrients, low organic matter.
what_to_do: Compare with a healthy patch
Ask for a soil test before adding fertiliser
expert_note: A soil test shows what the field really needs.

name: Iron shortage
looks_like: Newest leaves turn yellow or whitish while veins stay green.
favoured_by: Alkaline or chalky soils, waterlogging.
what_to_do: Check drainage
Ask the officer about the right correction for your soil
expert_note: Confirm with a soil test before treating.
